India-New Delhi
  
  
**Organization**
SE/HSD Department of Health Systems Development
  
  
**Schedule**
Full-time
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings.
  
  
**Area of expertise**
Roster of International consultant – Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance and/or laboratory strengthening for AMR
  
  
**Purpose of consultancy**
The WHO Regional Office for South-East Asia is establishing a roster of qualified consultants who may be engaged for specific assignments to strengthen national and regional AMR surveillance, clinical microbiology services and laboratory systems. Assignments may cover surveillance design and assessment; implementation and reporting through the Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System (GLASS); bacteriology and mycology capacity; diagnostic stewardship; laboratory networks and quality systems; data quality, analysis, interpretation and visualization; One Health and genomic surveillance; capacity development; operational research; and translation of surveillance evidence into policy and programme action.
  
  
Depending on the individual Terms of Reference, consultants will provide technical assistance for planning, implementation, analysis and reporting using WHO tools, standards and recommendations. They may also contribute to evidence-based technical guidance, protocols, standard operating procedures, training packages and implementation tools.
  
  
**Background**
Antimicrobial resistance is a major public health and development challenge in the WHO South-East Asia Region. Member States need timely, representative and quality-assured data on resistance patterns and antimicrobial use to guide national action plans, clinical and public health interventions, laboratory strategies, stewardship, infection prevention and control, and resource allocation.
  
  
Reliable laboratory systems are essential for effective AMR surveillance, including accurate bacterial and fungal identification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, diagnostic stewardship, specimen referral, quality management and standardized data flows. WHO supports Member States, country offices and partners to strengthen sustainable surveillance and laboratory systems aligned with WHO standards and GLASS. This roster will help WHO SEARO identify specialists for time-bound regional or country assignments based on emerging needs.
  
  
**Deliverables**
Under The Overall Guidance Of WHO Technical Unit, Consultants May Be Requested To Perform One Or More Of The Following Assignments (a More Specific Terms Of Reference (TORs), Including The Exact Deliverables, Duration Of Assignment And Place Of Assignment Will Be Shared With The Selected Candidate At The Time Of Hiring For a Specific Assignment):
  
  
****Deliverable 1: Surveillance and laboratory assessment.****
Conduct desk or country assessment of AMR surveillance systems, data flows, governance arrangements, indicators, data quality, bacteriology and mycology capacity, laboratory networks, diagnostic stewardship and reporting processes, with prioritized and feasible recommendations
  
  
****Deliverable 2: Technical products and implementation tools.****
Design assignment-specific protocols, standard operating procedures, data dictionaries, validation checklists, surveillance tools, indicator frameworks, laboratory-strengthening plans, survey materials, diagnostic-stewardship tools, guidance documents or One Health implementation products
  
  
****Deliverable 3: Data and analytical outputs.****
Develop cleaned or validated datasets; statistical, microbiological or genomic analyses; reproducible code or pipelines; tables, figures, maps, dashboards or visualization specifications; interpretation notes; and quality documentation, as applicable
  
  
****Deliverable 4: Laboratory and diagnostic products.****
Adapt guidance documents, training packages and tools for clinical bacteriology and mycology; laboratory quality management; antimicrobial susceptibility testing; external quality assurance; specimen referral; laboratory networks; and diagnostic stewardship.
  
  
****Deliverable 5: Capacity-development package.****
Develop training needs findings, curricula, presentations, exercises, job aids, workshop or webinar facilitation, mentoring records and a brief evaluation of learning and follow-up needs.
  
  
****Deliverable 6: Reporting and knowledge products.****
Prepare GLASS submission-related outputs, national or regional surveillance reports, laboratory-capacity reports, policy briefs, technical reports, manuscripts, systematic reviews, presentations or other communication products.
  
  
****Educational Qualifications****
**Qualifications, experience, skills and languages**
**Essential:**
**Band level B:**
A first university degree or medical degree in epidemiology, public health, medicine, clinical microbiology, laboratory sciences, biostatistics, statistics, mathematical modelling, health informatics, data science, computer science, bioinformatics, veterinary public health, environmental health, pharmacy, health economics or another field relevant to the assignment.
  
  
**Band level C:**
An advanced university degree or medical degree with postgraduate specialization in one of the fields listed above or another field relevant to the assignment.
  
  
Desirable: Additional postgraduate training, specialization or professional certification relevant to the technical profile, such as clinical microbiology, bacteriology, mycology, field epidemiology, laboratory quality management, diagnostic stewardship, data analytics, geographic information systems, genomic epidemiology, health information systems, monitoring and evaluation, or adult learning.
  
  
****Experience****
Essential
  
  
Band level B: At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in one or more of the technical profiles advertised.
  
  
**Band Level C:**

* At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in one or more of the advertised technical profiles.
* Demonstrated experience producing high-quality, assignment-relevant outputs such as surveillance assessments, protocols, analytical products, laboratory tools, technical reports, training packages, dashboards, scientific publications or policy products.
* For laboratory-focused assignments, essential experience may include one or more of the following:
* Implementation of recognized antimicrobial susceptibility testing standards, such as CLSI or EUCAST.
* Microbiological proficiency testing or external quality-assurance programmes.
* Bacteriology or mycology laboratory assessments and laboratory-system strengthening.
* Mycological diagnosis, diagnostic stewardship or laboratory quality management.

Desirable
  
  

* Experience with AMR surveillance and GLASS-related methods, tools or reporting.
* Experience working with ministries of health, national AMR programmes, public health institutes, reference laboratories, academic institutions or One Health coordination mechanisms.
* Experience in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in the WHO South-East Asia Region.
* Experience with WHO, another United Nations entity or an international public health organization.
* Experience facilitating multidisciplinary or multisectoral work and transferring skills to national teams.
* Experience implementing infectious-disease surveys or clinical research studies in accordance with good clinical and data-management practices.
* A publication record in peer-reviewed journals or authorship of technical guidance, national reports, research proposals, systematic reviews or evidence-synthesis products.
* Experience developing and applying bioinformatics pipelines, where relevant to the assignment.

**Essential**
**Skills and knowledge**

* Advanced knowledge and competence in at least one advertised technical profile, with a sound understanding of public health surveillance or laboratory-system principles relevant to the assignment.
* Ability to apply relevant WHO standards, methods and tools to national or regional contexts.
* Ability to analyse complex information, assure data or laboratory quality, interpret findings and formulate practical recommendations.
* Excellent technical writing, presentation and communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to technical and policy audiences.
* Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary settings and to deliver quality outputs within agreed timelines.
* For laboratory-focused assignments, essential competencies may include quality-assured microbiological testing, assessment of bacteriology or mycology laboratories, and design or implementation of external quality-assurance programmes.

Desirable
  
  

* Knowledge of GLASS, national AMR surveillance systems, One Health surveillance and relevant laboratory standards.
* Knowledge of laboratory networks and specimen-referral systems in resource-limited settings and associated challenges.
* Proficiency in one or more relevant platforms or languages, such as R, R Markdown, R Shiny, Python, SQL, Power BI, DHIS2, geographic information systems, statistical software, laboratory information systems, web technologies or bioinformatics tools.
* Knowledge of data governance, privacy, security, interoperability and reproducible analytical practices.
* Knowledge of adult learning, training design, facilitation and mentoring approaches.

****Languages And Level Required****
Essential: Expert knowledge of English.
  
  
Desirable: Intermediate or expert knowledge of another official United Nations language or a language used in a WHO South-East Asia Region Member State, where relevant to the assignment.
  
  
**Location**
Consultancies may be: Home-based, Country-based, Regional Office-based, or a combination of remote and in-country support. The duty arrangement for each consultancy will be specified in the individual Terms of Reference.
  
  
**Travel**
The consultant may be expected to travel to one or more WHO South-East Asia Region Member States for country assessments, laboratory assessments, technical consultations, training or other assignment-related activities. Travel dates, locations and purpose will be specified in the individual Terms of Reference and arranged in accordance with applicable WHO policies.
  
  
**Remuneration and budget (travel costs are excluded)**
**Remuneration:**
Band level B and/or Band level C, as applicable to the assignment. The daily or monthly rate will be established in accordance with the applicable WHO consultant remuneration guidance and stated in the individual Terms of Reference.
  
  
**Living expenses:**
Not applicable for home-based work. When an assignment requires on-site presence or travel, applicable travel and subsistence arrangements will be specified separately in accordance with WHO policies.
  
  
**Expected duration of contract**
: Roster assignments may range from short inputs to several months, up to a maximum of 11 months per calendar year. Each individual Terms of Reference will specify the contract duration, number of working days and, for part-time assignments, the expected percentage or level of effort.

title: Head - Data M&E & Institutional Intelligence
description:
**ROLE PURPOSE**

RightWalk operates on the principle that 'what gets measured, gets governed.' This role owns the data spine of the organisation — the independent control room that tells every layer of RightWalk whether systems are working, outcomes are real, and learning is being captured. Critically, this function must be independent of the program teams whose performance it measures. Data inflation and incentive-driven reporting are existential threats to RightWalk's credibility. The Head – Data, M&E & Institutional Intelligence is the institutional conscience of the organisation's evidence.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Data and indicator architecture**

* Design and own the end-to-end data architecture: from field input to impact indicators — definitions, collection protocols, validation logic, and storage.
* Build common data dictionaries across programs and states.
* Ensure indicator definitions are clear, auditable and usable by teams.
* Align program indicators with donor reporting, government dashboards and internal learning needs.

**2. Dashboards and institutional intelligence**

* Build and maintain real-time dashboards and standard report packs for the CEO, state teams, and donors.
* Drive institutional intelligence: cross-state comparisons, learning loops, and evidence synthesis for policy refinement.
* Convert data into actionable intelligence for policy, program and product decisions.
* Manage the Knowledge Management function — evidence library, document repositories, and institutional memory.

**3. M&E systems and quality assurance**

* Lead the M&E framework: indicator design, sampling methodology, periodic evaluation cycles, and external evaluation partnerships.
* Own data governance — data quality audits, mystery beneficiary calls, red-flag dashboards, and anomaly detection.
* Lead and develop State M&E Leads (embedded in states, functionally reporting to this role).
* Conduct periodic verification, mystery beneficiary calls, red-flag reviews and quality audits.
* Maintain strict independence from Program and State teams — this role's credibility depends on it.

**4. Learning loops and evidence building**

* Ensure field learning feeds into policy redesign, process improvement and product updates.
* Support impact evaluation readiness and external evaluation partnerships.
* Produce public-good outputs — impact reports, evidence briefs, and external publications that build RightWalk's credibility.

**5. Data governance and ethics**

* Define data access, privacy, anonymisation and data security protocols with Tech and People teams.
* Ensure responsible handling of beneficiary, field and government data.
* Create data discipline without making teams feel they are entering a tax raid.

**WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE — SIX MONTHS**

* Organisation-wide M&E and data architecture drafted and adopted.
* A live dashboard exists that the CEO, State Directors, and donors can access — real-time, reliable, and action-oriented.
* Data quality audits are conducted every quarter; anomalies are surfaced, not suppressed.
* The organisation makes at least two key program design changes in direct response to M&E evidence.
* RightWalk publishes at least one credible external evidence brief that strengthens its policy positioning.

**WHAT THIS ROLE DOES NOT DO**

* Setting programmatic targets — that is the program team's domain.
* Managing field delivery or GDN operations.
* Policy authorship or advocacy strategy.
* Tech platform development (though close collaboration with Tech is essential).
* Sit under state programs whose performance it must assess.

**CANDIDATE PROFILE**

* **Experience:**
  10–16 years in M&E, data systems, evaluation, or research — ideally within development sector, government advisory, or research institutions.
* **Methods:**
  Strong quantitative and qualitative research skills — comfortable with both survey-based M&E and systems-level data architecture.
* **Tools:**
  Experience with MIS/dashboard design and BI tools (Power BI, Tableau, or equivalent).
* **Independence:**
  Track record of building independent M&E functions that are trusted by leadership and donors alike.
* **Orientation:**
  Governance mindset - more interested in data integrity than in making numbers look good.
* **Sector:**
  Exposure to government data systems, HMIS, DISE, or similar public data infrastructure

title: S&OP Lead and Demand Planner, India
description:
Campari Group today is a major player in the global branded spirits industry, with a portfolio of over 50 premium and super premium brands, marketed and distributed in over 190 markets around the world, with leading positions in Europe and the Americas.
  
  
Headquartered in Milan, Italy, Campari Group owns
**25**
plants worldwide and has its own distribution network in
**26**
countries, and employs approximately
**4,700**
people.
  
  
Shares of the parent company Davide Campari - Milano N.V. are listed on the Italian Stock Exchange since 2001. Campari Group is today the sixth-largest player worldwide in the premium spirits industry.
  
  
**General Description Of The Role**

* The Demand Planner plays a pivotal role for developing and coordinating the Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process across the market
* The role assumes full business process ownership to develop an operational demand forecast providing governance of process and system, ensuring overall compliance with the global and regional planning cycle and monthly activities
* The role is responsible for guaranteeing data integrity & aggregation to provide the volume forecast outlook for the regional Supply Chain team as well as the BU MD and Management Team as part of the S&OP decision making process
* The role is also the key business reference between the SC and the Business Unit, acting as the bridge between sales, marketing, operations, and finance to ensure products are available at the right time and cost.

**Key Responsibilities And Activities**

* Forecasting & Analysis
* Leading the Demand Planning processes.
* Develop accurate demand forecasts using historical sales data, market trends, and statistical models.
* Monitor forecast accuracy and adjust models based on real-time data.
* Identify demand patterns, seasonality, and market shifts to anticipate future needs.
* Collaborate with Supply Planning to balance supply and demand to avoid stockouts or excess inventory.
* Be responsible for BUs planning template (IBP/SAP) ensuring that the system is deployed, utilized fully and proper system settings are maintained. Keep responsibility for system maintenance and IT ticket management
* S&OP and Cross-Functional Collaboration
* Champion S&OP to drive the change management and continuous improvement across countries to achieve the S&OP vision, objectives, and desired benefits
* Be the Key reference point with regards to S&OP activities
* Work closely with sales, marketing, and operations to align forecasts with promotional activities and product launches.
* Provide insights to finance teams for budgeting and revenue planning.
* Act as a central point of communication across departments to ensure consistency in demand planning.
* Conduct ongoing training both process and system to Key Users in Sales, Marketing, FP&A & Local Supply teams to ensure full understanding of S&OP and the planning activities are performed in the correct manner
* Reporting & Communication
* Prepare regular demand reports for management, highlighting risks and opportunities.
* Communicate forecast changes and inventory implications to stakeholders.
* Support decision-making with data-driven insights.
* Own the forecast accuracy KPIs to ensure definition and measurement is fully embedded in each country and support analysis & reporting. Drive forecast accuracy, MAPE and BIAS targets with the local teams.
* Continuous Improvement
* Implement forecasting tools and software to enhance accuracy.
* Benchmark performance against industry standards.
* Drive process improvements in demand planning and supply chain efficiency

**Summary Of Experience**

* Minimum 5-10 years of proven Demand / Supply Chain Planning experience
* Strong knowledge of commercial forecasting methods, background in statistical forecast
* Experience of working with Demand Planning systems in a defined planning cycle required.
* Must have a strong understanding and experience of S&OP/IBP and demand management principles and processes coupled with end-to-end supply chain operational processes.
* Experience of introducing/working with supply chain solutions, software and systems is beneficial. SAP experience is highly desirable.
* Hands on experience of SAP IBP Demand Planning advantageous.

**Education / Professional Qualifications**

* College / University degree with a major in Supply Chain management and/or Commercial Business Management
* APICs certification a plus
* Oliver Wight or similar Sales & Operations Planning / Integrated Business Management certified courses a plus
* Fluent in English

**Personal Skillset**

* High communication skills and ability to engage with key stakeholders
* Ability to lead and influence
* Ability to educate business partners and to drive change
* Ability to anticipate risks or opportunities
* Out of the box thinking
* Ability to think in the future to deliver results through others
* Intercultural competence and team worker

**Our commitment to Diversity & Inclusion:**
At Campari Group we believe in building more value together, thus we see diversity in all forms as a source of enrichment. Our employment policies and practices ensure that we are committed to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment without regard to any individual’s race, religion, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or characteristics or expression, political affiliation or activity, age, veteran status, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by law.
  
  
Campari Group believes that fair compensation and equal opportunities are crucial for employees’ well-being, empowerment, and engagement. Our efforts to ensure fair pay have earned us the Fair Pay Certification by Fair Pay Workplace, an independent organization dedicated to dismantling pay disparities based on gender, race and their intersection.
  
  
Note to applicants:
  
  
Your application will be assessed based on your abilities, expertise, general knowledge and experience, not because of any confidential, proprietary or trade secret information you may possess. You must not disclose to Campari Group any such information. description:

External consultant

**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings.
  
  
**Area of expertise**
Roster of International consultant – Strategic planning, costing, monitoring, and evaluation for antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
  
  
**Purpose of consultancy**
The WHO South-East Asia Regional Office (SEARO) seeks to establish a roster of qualified consultants to provide technical support to Member States in the development, implementation, costing, monitoring, evaluation, review, and strengthening of National Action Plans (NAPs) on Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR).
  
  
Selected consultants may be engaged to support regional and country-level activities aligned with the Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance, the WHO SEARO Regional Roadmap on AMR 2025-2030, and the One Health approach.
  
  
**Background**
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains a major threat to public health, food security, economic development, and health system resilience. Countries in the WHO South-East Asia Region have developed and are implementing National Action Plans on AMR; however, varying levels of capacity, financing, governance, monitoring systems, and multisectoral coordination continue to challenge effective implementation.
  
  
To support Member States in strengthening AMR national programmes and advancing implementation of the WHO SEARO Regional Roadmap on AMR 2025-2030, WHO requires a roster of technical experts capable of providing specialized support across strategic planning, costing, resource mobilization, monitoring and evaluation, programme review, governance strengthening, and One Health coordination.
  
  
The roster will enable WHO to rapidly mobilize qualified experts to support national and regional priorities as needs arise.
  
  
**Deliverables**
Under The Overall Guidance Of WHO Technical Unit, Consultants May Be Requested To Perform One Or More Of The Following Assignments (a More Specific Terms Of Reference (TORs), Including The Exact Deliverables, Duration Of Assignment And Place Of Assignment Will Be Shared With The Selected Candidate At The Time Of Hiring For a Specific Assignment)
  
  
**Deliverable 1: National Action Plan Development and Revision**

* Conduct situational and strategic analyses.
* Facilitate stakeholder consultations and multisectoral engagement.
* Develop or update AMR National Action Plans.
* Prepare implementation frameworks and operational plans.
* Support national validation and endorsement processes.

**Deliverable 2: Costing, Budgeting and Financing**

* Develop costed implementation plans.
* Conduct budget and financing analyses.
* Estimate resource requirements and investment needs.
* Develop financing scenarios and sustainability plans.
* Prepare resource mobilization strategies and investment cases.
* Assess cost-saving potential, cost-effectiveness and return on investment for AMR interventions and implementation options.

**Deliverable 3: Monitoring, Evaluation and Accountability Frameworks**

* Develop theories of change and results frameworks.
* Design logical frameworks and performance indicators.
* Establish monitoring and reporting mechanisms.
* Develop accountability and learning frameworks.
* Design data collection and review tools

**Deliverable 4: Mid-Term and End-Term Reviews**

* Develop review methodologies and assessment tools.
* Conduct programme performance reviews.
* Facilitate stakeholder consultations and review workshops.
* Analyse implementation progress and bottlenecks.
* Produce review reports and recommendations.

**Deliverable 5: Capacity Development**

* Develop training materials and guidance documents.
* Deliver workshops and technical training sessions.
* Provide mentoring and coaching to national teams.
* Strengthen national capacity in planning, costing, monitoring and evaluation.

**Deliverable 6: Reporting and Policy Products**

* Prepare technical reports and progress reports.
* Develop policy briefs and evidence summaries.
* Produce national and regional assessment reports.
* Develop strategic planning and investment documents.

**Educational Qualifications**
**Qualifications, experience, skills and languages**
**Essential**
**For Band level B**
: A first university degree or medical degree in one or more of the following fields: Public Health, Health Policy and Management, Health Economics, Epidemiology, Monitoring and Evaluation, International Development, Health Systems Strengthening, One Health, Veterinary Public Health, Environmental Health, Public Administration, and/or Business Administration.
  
  
**For Band level C**
: An advanced university degree or medical degree with postgraduate specialization in one of the fields listed above or another field relevant to the assignment.
  
  
Desirable: Additional postgraduate training or professional certification relevant to the technical profile.
  
  
**Experience**
Essential:
  
  
**For Band Level B**

* At least five years of of progressively responsible experience in one or more of the advertised technical profiles.
* Demonstrated experience supporting programme planning, monitoring, evaluation, policy development, or health systems strengthening
* Experience working with governments, international organizations, development partners, or academic institutions

**For Band Level C**

* At least ten years of progressively responsible experience in one or more of the advertised technical profiles.
* Demonstrated expertise in strategic planning, programme review, financing, monitoring and evaluation, health financing, policy development, or One Health implementation.

**Desirable**

* Experience supporting national or regional programmes in low- and middle-income countries, particularly in the WHO South-East Asia Region.
* Experience working with WHO, UN agencies, development partners, or government institutions is desirable.
* Experience facilitating multidisciplinary or multisectoral work and transferring skills to national teams.
* Publication record in peer-reviewed journals or authorship of technical guidance, national reports or evidence-synthesis products.

**Skills/Knowledge**
Essential
  
  

* Expertise in one or more of the following areas: AMR policy and strategy development, National Action Plan development and revision, Health economics, costing and budgeting, Resource mobilization and investment case development, Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL), Results-based management, Programme performance assessment, Public health planning, One Health implementation, Governance and multisectoral coordination, Facilitation of national reviews and assessments, Strategic planning and operational planning, and Development of policy briefs and technical reports.
* Ability to apply relevant WHO standards, methods and tools to national or regional contexts.
* Ability to analyse complex information, assure data quality, interpret findings and formulate practical recommendations.
* Excellent technical writing, presentation and communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to technical and policy audiences.

Desirable
  
  

* Excellent facilitation and stakeholder engagement skills.
* Ability to work independently and meet deadlines.
* Ability to work effectively in multicultural and multidisciplinary settings and to deliver quality outputs within agreed timelines.
* Knowledge of adult learning, training design, facilitation and mentoring approaches.

**Languages And Level Required**
Essential: Expert knowledge of English
  
  
Desirable: Intermediate or expert knowledge of another official United Nations language or a language used in a WHO South-East Asia Region Member State, where relevant to the assignment.
  
  
**Location**

* Consultancies may be: Home-based, Country-based, Regional Office-based,, or a combination of remote and in-country support.
* The duty arrangement for each consultancy will be specified in the individual Terms of Reference.

**Travel**
The consultant may be expected to travel to one or more WHO South-East Asia Region Member States for country assessments, technical consultations, training or other assignment-related activities. Travel dates, locations and purpose will be specified in the individual Terms of Reference and arranged in accordance with applicable WHO policies.

**Expected duration of contract:**
Roster assignments may range from short inputs to several months, up to a maximum of 11 months per calendar year. Each individual Terms of Reference will specify the contract duration, number of working days and, for part-time assignments, the expected percentage or level of effort.

title: Geospatial Intelligence Analyst
description:
**Role Highlights**

* Role: Geospatial Intelligence Analyst
* Department: ISR (Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance)
* Location: New Delhi, India
* Reports to: Operations Lead, ISR Analytics
* Working type: Hybrid
* Employment is subject to applicable security screening (incl. SUPO, where required)

The Mission of the Geospatial Intelligence Analyst
  
  
As Geospatial Intelligence Analyst, you will be the bridge between ICEYE's world-leading SAR satellite data and the defence and intelligence customers who depend on it to make mission-critical decisions. Your core work is transforming complex radar and electro-optical imagery into precise, timely intelligence reports and operational insights — applying rigorous imagery intelligence tradecraft to answer real questions in high-stakes environments. Beyond the analysis itself, you will brief VIP and expert audiences, train customer teams to independently harness ICEYE's capabilities, and collaborate with product and engineering teams to shape the next generation of ISR tools and workflows.
  
  
Who are we?
  
  
ICEYE delivers space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) capabilities to governments and allied nations. This includes sovereign and turnkey ISR missions leveraging ICEYE's world-leading synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite technology, as well as access to data from the world's largest SAR satellite constellation. These capabilities enable partners to detect and respond to critical changes anywhere on Earth with unprecedented speed and accuracy – day or night and in any weather, supported by ultra high-resolution imagery and high-frequency revisits.
  
  
As a trusted partner for defense, intelligence, security, and maritime domain awareness, ICEYE's near real-time data creates a tactical advantage for mission-critical operations. ICEYE operates internationally with offices in Finland, Poland, Spain, Japan, the UAE, Greece, Germany, and the US. The company has more than 900 employees, inspired by the shared vision of improving life on Earth by becoming the global source of truth in Earth Observation.
  
  
**Day To Day Responsibilities**

* Conduct SAR and EO imagery interpretation.
* Deliver analysis outputs and intelligence reports for defence & intelligence users.
* Conduct briefings and demonstrations to VIPs and expert audiences alike.
* Train, and enable customers to independently use ICEYE’s systems and analytical tools.
* Contribute to ISR product development by implementing new analysis, dissemination. and integration workflows in collaboration with product and engineering teams.

**Requirements**
Must have skills
  
  

* Bachelor’s degree or higher in relevant fields (e.g. geography, geoinformatics, military studies).
* Strong geospatial foundation; experience in e.g. QGIS, ArcGIS.
* Ability to operate in a fast-paced operational environment as part of a tightly-nit team in field deployments.
* Excellent communication, social, and presentation skills; comfortable with diverse and senior audiences.
* Experience in SAR and EO imagery interpretation or experience in GEONT, IMINT disciplines highly desirable.
* Comfortable working under pressure, on-site, and during prolonged deployments.
* Experience in military or defense sectors is strongly preferred.
* Subject matter expertise in naval, ground or air domains highly desirable.
* Programming (Python) and utilizing AI/ML frameworks to develop applications.
* Team player with a good sense of humor.
* High integrity and resiliency, strong ownership, and continuous learning mindset.

Nice to have skills
  
  

* Fluent in English.
* Ability to travel frequently and sometimes on short notice.
* Geospatial / ISR expertise required; either geospatial or intelligence foundations must be strong
* Must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

Application process
  
  

* Talent Acquisition Interview
* Hiring Manager Interview
* Technical Interview (onsite or virtual), including a Technical Challenge
* Hiring Team Interview
* Offer Decision

Working at ICEYE
  
  
At ICEYE, you’ll join a diverse and highly engaged team united by the ambition to make the impossible possible. As a global scale-up, we combine speed and ambition with the opportunity to take real ownership from day one. Your growth, wellbeing, and success are a priority, with continuous professional development, training opportunities, and a culture where collaboration is how we win.
  
  
How We Work (Our Values)
  
  
**Make the impossible possible:**
We set ambitious goals and stay calm under pressure. We bring grit, optimism, and ownership when things get hard, and we keep moving until we find a way.
  
  

* Be curious: Go deep, ask questions, listen carefully, and think critically. Understand the “why” behind decisions.
* See the big picture: Stay close to what’s happening across the company so you can make better decisions. Consider how your work affects others.
* Drive effective teamwork: Create psychological safety, invite different perspectives, and build inclusive teams. There are no bad questions.
* Act as one team: We win together. We match tasks to the right owner and stay agile as priorities shift.
* Have fun: What we do matters—and it should be enjoyable. Celebrate progress, take pride in results, and share the wins.

**Benefits**
Our benefits are designed to support your health and wellbeing—at work and beyond. We keep improving them based on employee feedback, and offerings vary by location. Talent Acquisition will confirm what applies for this role and location during the process.
  
  
Our commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion
  
  
We want ICEYE to be a place where people can be themselves and do great work. Different backgrounds and perspectives make us stronger, which is why we work to create an environment where people feel included, respected, and able to speak up. Whatever your background, we want you to bring your authentic self to the table.
  
  
We’re committed to fair, inclusive hiring and equal opportunity. Everyone is welcome to apply. If you need any adjustments or support during the recruitment process, tell us—we’ll do our best to help.
  
  
Apply now to start your ICEYE journey, and help us continue to make the impossible possible together. Read more about ICEYE and working with us at iceye.com

title: Scientific Computing / Research Engineering Expert — Earth Sciences
description:
**About Turing:**

* Turing is one of the world’s fastest-growing AI companies, accelerating the advancement and deployment of powerful AI systems.
* Turing helps customers in two ways: Working with the world’s leading AI labs to advance frontier model capabilities in thinking, reasoning, coding, agentic behavior, multimodality, multilinguality, STEM and frontier knowledge; and leveraging that work to build real-world AI systems that solve mission-critical priorities for companies.

**Role Overview:**

* We are seeking experienced Earth Sciences experts to develop realistic, terminal-based scientific and computational tasks for a frontier AI training and evaluation initiative.
* In this role, you will design challenging scientific tasks involving climate science, atmospheric processes, geophysics, oceanography, geology, hydrology, remote sensing, and environmental modeling. You will build reproducible computational workflows that require AI agents to analyze scientific datasets, execute code, run simulations, troubleshoot technical issues, and generate objectively verifiable scientific outputs.

**What you'll do:**

* Design realistic, multi-step scientific tasks based on authentic Earth Sciences, climate, geospatial, environmental, and geophysical research workflows.
* Prepare and process scientific datasets involving climate, weather, atmospheric conditions, oceanography, geology, hydrology, satellite imagery, and environmental systems.
* Develop computational tasks involving geospatial analysis, time-series processing, numerical modeling, interpolation, forecasting, remote sensing, and environmental risk analysis.
* Build reproducible, terminal-based computational environments using scientific libraries, command-line tools, and appropriate dependencies.
* Develop expert reference solutions using Python, R, Bash, Julia, or domain-specific scientific software.
* Create automated tests and evaluation criteria to verify scientific correctness, numerical accuracy, spatial and temporal consistency, and reproducibility.
* Validate coordinate reference systems, measurement units, timestamps, missing-data handling, uncertainty, and scientific assumptions.
* Troubleshoot technical issues involving geospatial projections, large scientific datasets, software dependencies, computational performance, and numerical stability.
* Ensure tasks require meaningful multi-step scientific reasoning and cannot be solved through simple shortcuts or hard-coded outputs.
* Document dataset sources, computational workflows, expected outputs, edge cases, and scientific limitations.

**What we're looking for:**

* Ph.D., postdoctoral experience, or equivalent advanced technical experience in Earth Sciences, Climate Science, Atmospheric Science, Geophysics, Oceanography, Geology, Hydrology, Environmental Science, or a closely related discipline.
* Strong programming skills in Python, R, Bash, Julia, or another relevant scientific programming language.
* Hands-on experience working in Linux and terminal-based computational environments.
* Practical expertise in at least one major area: scientific data processing, numerical modeling, geospatial analysis, climate modeling, remote sensing, or environmental data analysis.
* Strong understanding of spatial datasets, time-series analysis, scientific modeling, numerical accuracy, uncertainty, and data quality control.
* Experience working with real-world scientific datasets, including geospatial, climate, atmospheric, oceanographic, geological, or hydrological data.
* Ability to independently develop, execute, debug, and validate reproducible scientific computational workflows.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to identify scientific inaccuracies, data inconsistencies, and computational errors.
* Ability to design objective validation methods and clearly document technical solutions and scientific assumptions.

**Nice to have:**

* Experience with scientific computing and geospatial libraries such as NumPy, pandas, SciPy, xarray, rasterio, GeoPandas, Cartopy, GDAL, or similar tools.
* Familiarity with scientific data formats such as NetCDF, HDF5, GeoTIFF, shapefiles, GRIB, and other geospatial or environmental data formats.
* Experience working with climate, weather, oceanographic, seismic, satellite, hydrological, or geological datasets.
* Familiarity with Docker, Conda, Git, CI/CD pipelines, and automated testing frameworks.
* Experience using high-performance computing (HPC) environments or processing large-scale scientific datasets.
* Experience with Earth-system models, environmental forecasting, remote sensing applications, or geophysical simulations.
* Research software engineering experience, including developing scientific tools, simulation pipelines, or reproducible research workflows.
* Experience developing or evaluating AI coding agents, terminal-based agents, scientific benchmarks, or automated grading systems.
* Publications, research contributions, or open-source development experience in Earth or Environmental Sciences.
* Prior experience in AI training, scientific quality control, benchmark development, or evaluation programs.

**Offer Details:**

* **Commitments Required:**
  At least 4 hours per day and minimum 40 hours per week with overlap of 4 hours with PST.
* **Employment type :**
  Contractor assignment (no medical/paid leave)
* **Duration of contract :**
  4 week [expected start date is next week]

description:
**Contractual Arrangement**
External consultant

Full-time
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device's system settings.
  
  
**Area of expertise**
Roster of International consultant – Antimicrobial Use (AMU), Access and/or Stewardship
  
  
**Purpose of consultancy**
The WHO South-East Asia Regional Office (SEARO) seeks to establish a roster of qualified consultants to provide technical support to Member States in strengthening antimicrobial stewardship, improving access to quality-assured antimicrobials, optimizing antimicrobial use, strengthening pharmaceutical governance and regulatory systems, monitoring antimicrobial consumption, and implementing One Health approaches to address antimicrobial resistance.
  
  
Selected consultants may be engaged to support regional and country-level activities aligned with the Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance, the 2024 United Nations General Assembly Political Declaration on AMR, the WHO SEARO Regional Roadmap on AMR 2025-2030, WHO AWaRe guidance, Universal Health Coverage goals, national AMR action plans, and relevant WHO guidance, standards and toolkits on antimicrobial use surveillance, antimicrobial stewardship, equitable access to quality-assured antimicrobials, and responsible antimicrobial use across human health and One Health contexts.
  
  
**Background**
AMR continues to threaten public health and health system resilience across the WHO South-East Asia Region. Despite progress in implementing national action plans, countries continue to face challenges in responsible antimicrobial use, equitable access to quality-assured antimicrobials, stewardship capacity, AMU surveillance, regulatory oversight and pharmaceutical governance. Strengthening AWaRe implementation, stewardship programmes, surveillance systems and One Health collaboration remains a regional priority under the WHO SEARO Regional Roadmap on AMR 2025–2030. A roster of technical experts will help WHO rapidly support Member States with specialized expertise as needs arise.
  
  
**Deliverables**
Under the overall guidance of the WHO technical unit, consultants may be requested to perform one or more of the following assignments. A more specific Terms of Reference, including exact deliverables, duration, and place of assignment, will be issued at the time of contracting.
  
  
**Deliverable 1: Antimicrobial Use (AMU) Surveillance and Analytics**
Establish or strengthen AMU surveillance systems, including methods, protocols, data collection, analysis, reporting, dashboards, multisectoral integration, and technical recommendations.
  
  
**Deliverable 2: Antimicrobial Stewardship Programme Development and Implementation**
Develop and implement AMS strategies, programmes, tools and quality-improvement measures, including AWaRe implementation and interventions to improve prescribing practices.
  
  
**Deliverable 3: Access to Antimicrobials and Shortage Management**
Assess antimicrobial availability, affordability, accessibility, quality, shortages, procurement and supply-chain systems, and develop strategies to improve access, prevent stockouts, strengthen supply security, and ensure equitable access to essential antibiotics.
  
  
**Deliverable 4: Regulatory Systems and Pharmaceutical Governance**
Review antimicrobial regulatory and policy frameworks, assess prescribing, dispensing, sales and marketing practices, and support stronger regulations, quality assurance, licensing, prescription-only policies and implementation recommendations.
  
  
**Deliverable 5: One Health Antimicrobial Use Optimization**
Support One Health approaches to optimize antimicrobial use across human, animal, food production and environmental sectors, including multisectoral coordination, integrated monitoring, consultations, and implementation of responsible-use strategies and action plans.
  
  
**Deliverable 6: Capacity Development**
Develop and deliver AMS/AMU training, mentoring, awareness and behaviour-change activities, and strengthen institutional capacity for stewardship, surveillance, regulation and access programmes.
  
  
**Deliverable 7: Monitoring, Evaluation and Programme Performance Assessment**
Monitor and evaluate AMS, AMU, access and governance programmes, including indicators, reporting systems, performance reviews, lessons learned and recommendations for strengthening and sustainability.
  
  
**Deliverable 8: Technical Guidance, Research and Knowledge Products**
Develop technical guidance, reports, evidence summaries, research and knowledge products to support policy, investment, implementation and dissemination.
  
  
**Educational Qualifications**
**Qualifications, experience, skills and languages**
**Essential**
**For Band level B**
**:**
A first university degree or medical degree in one or more of the following fields: Medicine, Pharmacy, Public Health, Infectious Diseases, Clinical and/or Infectious Disease Pharmacology, Epidemiology, Veterinary Medicine, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Health Policy and Management, Health Systems Strengthening, One Health, and Related disciplines.
  
  
**For Band level C:**
An advanced university degree or medical degree with postgraduate specialization in one of the fields listed above or another field relevant to the assignment.
  
  
Desirable
  
  

* Doctoral degree
* Board certification or postgraduate specialization relevant to the technical profile
* Professional certification related to AMS, public health, epidemiology, health systems, medicines regulation, pharmaceutical policy, or monitoring and evaluation.

**Experience**
Essential
  
  
**For Band Level B**

* At least five years of of progressively responsible experience in one or more of the advertised technical profiles.
* Experience supporting AMS programmes, antimicrobial use monitoring, pharmaceutical systems, policy development, surveillance, or public health programmes.

**For Band Level C**

* At least ten years of progressively responsible experience in one or more of the advertised technical profiles.
* Demonstrated expertise in antimicrobial stewardship, antimicrobial use surveillance, pharmaceutical governance, access to medicines, regulatory strengthening, policy development, or One Health implementation.

Desirable
  
  

* Experience supporting programmes in low- and middle-income countries.
* Experience in WHO South-East Asia Region Member States.
* Experience working with WHO, UN agencies, governments, development partners, professional societies, academic institutions, or medicines regulatory authorities.
* Experience facilitating multidisciplinary and multisectoral initiatives.
* Publication record in peer-reviewed journals or technical guidance documents.

**Skills/Knowledge**
Essential
  
  

* Expertise in one or more of the advertised technical profiles.
* Knowledge of WHO AWaRe classification and implementation approaches.
* Knowledge of antimicrobial stewardship and rational use of medicines.
* Knowledge of pharmaceutical systems and medicines regulation.
* Experience with antimicrobial use and consumption monitoring.
* Ability to apply WHO standards, methods, and tools.
* Strong analytical, technical writing, and communication skills.
* Ability to analyse complex information and develop practical recommendations.
* Experience facilitating stakeholder consultations and technical discussions.

Desirable
  
  

* Experience in behavioural science and behaviour change interventions.
* Knowledge of digital health solutions and data analytics.
* Knowledge of forecasting, quantification, and supply chain management.
* Experience in training, facilitation, mentoring, and adult learning approaches.

**Languages And Level Required**
Essential: Expert knowledge of English.
  
  
Desirable: Intermediate or expert knowledge of another official United Nations language or a language used in a WHO South-East Asia Region Member State, where relevant to the assignment.
  
  
**Location**

* The duty arrangement for each consultancy will be specified in the individual Terms of Reference.

**Travel**
The consultant may be expected to travel to one or more WHO South-East Asia Region Member States for country assessments, technical consultations, training or other assignment-related activities. Travel dates, locations and purpose will be specified in the individual Terms of Reference and arranged in accordance with applicable WHO policies.

title: Specialist - Commercial Standards Claims & Contract
description:
**Job Description**
**Specialist — Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts is a Business Analyst and SME on the Customer Operations Transformation programme.**
The outcome is a clear, governed set of commercial policies — credit, claims, pricing and trade terms — and customer agreements that are standard, compliant and correctly executed in the systems; fewer and cleaner customer claims; lower invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage; and <1 Day Resolution wherever the process allows: fewer claims arising in the first place, and faster, controlled settlement for those that remain. Everything this role does serves that outcome.
  
  
The scope spans Commercial Standards, Claims and Contracts end to end — formulation and governance of credit, claims, pricing and trade-terms policies, policy exceptions and delegation of authority, the customer agreement and contract lifecycle (drafting, approval, activation, amendment and renewal), pricing, rebate, discount and promotion setup, accruals, claims intake, validation and settlement, proof of performance, and the controls that link agreed terms to what is invoiced and paid. The role designs across this scope as one process rather than as separate contract, promotion and claims solutions. It works with market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service and Collections teams, GBO, D&T, the SAP and Control Tower (Claims and Deduction platform) teams and third-party vendors.
  
  
The role combines 5 capabilities in one person. As an SME, they formulate, document the global commercial policies — credit policy (credit limits, payment terms, risk categories, blocks and releases), claims policy (eligibility, evidence, time limits, approval and write-off thresholds), and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount and rebate guardrails, price-change control) — and the standards and controls that make them work in practice. As a business analyst, they interrogate contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data, document current and target process, and write requirements to standard. As a subject matter expert, they bring the functional depth to act as design authority for the fragment and to challenge solutions that would not work in the markets. As a sprint or project owner, they take a scope fragment through design, test and deployment on a two to four week value drop cadence. As a process and technology expert, they translate commercial policy, contract terms and controls into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction capability, and the contract and trade promotion management toolset.
  
  
**The defining discipline of this role is designing claims out at source, not processing them faster.**
A quicker claim approval is a smaller prize than a contract term clear enough never to be disputed; a faster settlement is a smaller prize than a promotion set up correctly in the system so the customer never needs to claim. The postholder is expected to use the data to find where in the commercial process claims are created — an ambiguous contract clause, a non-standard trade term, a late or incorrect pricing or promotion setup, an accrual gap, a weak approval control — and design the fix upstream into commercial policy, standards, contract templates, deal approval and master data, as well as into the claims and settlement design.
  
  
**Understanding of markets and of upstream and downstream impact is central to the role.**
A claim usually starts life as a commercial negotiation; a contract term becomes a pricing condition, an accrual, an invoice and, if anything is misaligned, a deduction in Collections. The postholder is expected to know what happens on either side of their own process — from deal negotiation through to cash and the P&L — and to design accordingly.
  
  
**This is a transformation design and delivery role, not an operational one.**
The postholder does not negotiate customer deals, draft or approve individual contracts, validate or settle individual claims, or manage customer relationships; that stays with market Commercial, Legal, GBO and BPO run teams. The role changes how that work is done — including the commercial policies, standards, contract templates, reason codes, analytics and controls that let run teams find and remove causes in BAU. The role formulates and recommends policy; final approval sits with the relevant policy owners and governance forums.
  
  
The role works independently within an agreed frame set by the workstream lead, gathers its own data, forms its own view and brings recommendations rather than questions. Where a Senior Specialist is assigned on the same fragment, it works under their design direction. Decisions are expected to be based on evidence rather than opinion, and every artefact is expected to meet the programme documentation, taxonomy and quality standards, including BPQMS.
  
  
**Analyse commercial terms, contracts and claims performance and baseline the problem — 25%.**
Document current-state credit, claims and pricing policies, commercial standards, contract lifecycle and claims processes across markets and identify variation from the global standard. Build the process, trade-terms and claim-type taxonomy and interrogate the data directly at portfolio level — customer agreements and terms, pricing and promotion conditions, accruals versus actuals, claims volume, value, ageing and rejection rates, invalid deductions, write-offs and trade-spend leakage — to baseline the problem per market and size the opportunity. Perform gap analysis between current process, commercial policy, contract terms, platform capability, controls and the target operating model, separating structural design issues from operational backlog. Support business-rule validation, master-data requirements and policy analysis. Aim for validated current-state documentation and a defensible baseline that will stand up to audit.
  
  
**Formulate commercial policies and standards, and design claims out at source — 25%.**
Support future-state design aligned to the global standard, always designing for the cause rather than the symptom. Formulate, document and maintain the global commercial policies the design depends on — credit policy (credit limits and risk categorisation, payment terms, credit blocks and release authority), claims policy (claim eligibility, evidence and proof-of-performance requirements, submission time limits, validation, approval and write-off thresholds) and pricing governance (price-setting and approval, discount, rebate and promotion guardrails, price-change control and margin protection) — with a clear policy-exception and delegation-of-authority framework, and take them through the governance forums for approval. Translate policy into the standards that operationalise it: standard trade-terms structures, contract and agreement templates, clause libraries, deal approval and delegation-of-authority rules, and the minimum data a contract must carry to be executed correctly in the systems. Use the baseline to show where claims are created — contract ambiguity, non-standard terms, pricing and promotion setup, accruals, proof of performance, master data — and design the fix upstream. Design the interventions: standard contract-to-condition setup, automated accruals and settlement, validated claim intake, reason-code frameworks and claims workflow. Prepare business requirements, functional specifications, process flows, business rules and user stories. Facilitate design workshops and document outcomes and decisions. Assess process, policy, financial and control impacts, and define how policy compliance will be monitored.
  
  
Deliver the outcome: standard contracts, fewer claims and <1 Day Resolution — 20%. Design for, and evidence, policy adoption and compliance across markets, an increase in contracts on standard terms and templates, fewer policy exceptions, a reduction in claims volume, aged claims, invalid deductions and trade-spend leakage, and movement toward <1 Day Resolution for appropriate claims and queries. Shape the build-out of SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, Control Tower claims and deduction functionality, and contract and trade promotion management tooling as the primary levers on the outcome. Define the measures with the business owner, monitor post-go-live performance against the baseline, and recommend and, where owned, implement continuous improvements to the design. This is the accountability every other accountability serves.
  
  
**Own testing, deployment and adoption through the value drops — 20%.**
Translate requirements into working design on SAP, Control Tower and the contract and trade promotion management toolset with D&T, system integrators and vendors. Define and review test scenarios, support SIT and UAT, and manage defect resolution with business users. Break the work into fragments that can be delivered on the value drop cadence, and own the backlog, dependencies and risks for the fragment. Support deployment, hypercare and business readiness, and hand over up-to-date commercial standards, contract templates, process documentation, SOPs, controls and training materials to the run teams. Aim for SIT and UAT completed with minimal post-go-live defects and a clean handover into run.
  
  
**Manage delivery discipline and enable across the programme — 10%.**
Track requirements, risks, assumptions, dependencies and decisions throughout the lifecycle, and escalate early and precisely when the frame is wrong. Act as a trusted partner to market Commercial, Revenue Growth Management, Sales Finance, Credit, Legal, Internal Control, Customer Service, GBO, D&T and vendors, and coach business users through testing, deployment and adoption. Enable the adjacent workstreams — Order-to-Invoice, Collections, Claims & Receivables, Customer Service and Supply — by surfacing cross-boundary impact before it becomes a deployment defect, and by handing design-level root causes to the workstream that owns them.
  
  

* Commercial Standards, Claims & Contracts domain depth and business analysis, on a broad Customer Operations base. Real SME depth in commercial policy and customer contracts — credit policy and credit risk, claims policy, pricing governance, trade-terms structures, rebates, discounts and promotions, contract lifecycle management, accruals, and claims validation and settlement — sufficient to act as design authority and to write policy that is clear, enforceable and auditable, combined with strong business-analysis craft: process mapping, requirements gathering, gap analysis, functional-specification writing, user stories and workshop facilitation. Understands how claims and deductions are created across the commercial and Order to Cash process, and how contract wording, deal approval, pricing and promotion setup, master data and accruals drive them. Built on a general understanding of Customer Operations end-to-end (Order to Cash, Commercial and Supply) and of how markets actually work, including upstream and downstream impact. Knows Consumer Products industry standards and the realities of Beer, Wine & Spirits — distributor and wholesaler concentration, complex customer agreements, promotional and trade-spend claims, and route-to-market and regulatory constraints on trade terms. Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards.
* Data, technology and delivery discipline. Comfortable interrogating contract, trade-terms, accrual, claims and deduction data directly, and translating requirements into working design on SAP pricing, condition contracts and settlement management, the Control Tower claims and deduction platform, and the supporting contract and trade promotion management toolset. Understands the platform, the data model, the business rules, workflow and approval logic, and the operating model — retained, GBO and BPO — beneath the process. Strong on test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT), business readiness and hypercare, and on risk, issue and dependency management. Data-driven by instinct — baselines the problem, quantifies the opportunity and lets the evidence settle the argument. Able to prioritise across concurrent workstreams and deadlines.
* Design-for-prevention rigour, stakeholder influence and adaptability. Relentless about cause over symptom in design — not satisfied with automating a workaround when the claim could be designed out through a clearer standard, contract or setup. Strong stakeholder management and influencing across a global and local matrix, including senior Commercial, Finance and Legal stakeholders and policy governance forums, and consultative by default: frames the problem before prescribing and drives stakeholders toward aligned design decisions. Clear communicator, and able to manage conflict to a resolution rather than let it stall a decision. Comfortable being redeployed: arrives in an unfamiliar market or process, orients fast, and adds value quickly. Resilient, collaborative, and a visible role model for Diageo’s values.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience in Finance, Business, Commercial, Law, Operations, IT or a related discipline.
* Working knowledge of Diageo BPQMS standards. Business-analysis, Agile / Scrum or Lean Six Sigma credentials are an advantage; familiarity with SAP pricing, condition contracts or settlement management, Control Tower or similar claims and deduction platforms, or contract lifecycle or trade promotion management tools is a plus.

**Experience — Essential**

* Overall. 10+ years spanning transformation, business analysis and consultative experience, with a strong core of business analysis and SME design work in large-scale process transformation.
* Subject matter expertise. Deep functional understanding of credit, claims and pricing policy, commercial terms, customer contracts and agreements, trade promotions and claims within a Commercial and Order-to-Cash environment — someone who knows how claims and deductions are created by contract terms and commercial setup, and how standards and process should be designed to prevent them, not only the tooling. Operational exposure is useful context; the requirement is designing the process, not running it.
* Transformation. Experience in business process transformation, including current-state assessment and future-state operating model design, across the full lifecycle from design through testing, deployment and post-go-live stabilisation. Evidence of reducing claims, deductions, trade-spend leakage, cycle time or manual effort against a defensible baseline.
* Consultative. A track record of acting as a trusted business partner — framing the real problem, facilitating design decisions, aligning global and local stakeholders — and being measured on whether the business changed, not only on whether the deliverable shipped.
* Technology. Experience translating business requirements into functional specifications and solution design with D&T, system integrators and vendors, including test planning and defect management (SIT / UAT). SAP pricing, condition contracts or settlement management, Control Tower, or comparable contract, trade promotion or claims platform exposure is an advantage.
* Industry. FMCG or Consumer Products experience is essential. Beer, Wine & Spirits experience is strongly preferred.
* General understanding of Customer Operations end to end — OTC, Commercial and Supply — and of how markets actually operate, including upstream and downstream impact.

**Experience — Desirable**

* Experience formulating and governing commercial policy — credit, claims and pricing governance — and the standards beneath it: trade-terms frameworks, contract templates, clause libraries and deal approval policies — across multiple markets.
* Exposure to contract lifecycle management, trade promotion management, or claims and settlement automation, including AI-led claim validation and matching.
* Experience designing reason-code frameworks and claims analytics that let run teams identify and remove the causes of claims and deductions.
* Experience defining what must be global standard versus what requires market localisation.

**About Us**

Data aggregation and cleaning, power queries, data modelling, Power BI visualization design, programming in DAX, and mapping to Smartsheet.

* Demonstrate the ability to rapidly evaluate, learn and implement modern automation technologies (Power Automate, Python, AI-enabled workflows in line with Gartner AI governance policies, Power Automate and SharePoint integration) to improve operational efficiency, scalability, and user experience.
* Ability to execute at the highest level in fast-paced environment with multiple and competing, high-impact priorities. Independently drive results from start to finish.

* Maintain and enhance SharePoint sites supporting conference operations, including site structure, permissions, data management, document libraries, workflows, and user support. Implement improvements that drive collaboration, information accessibility, process efficiency, and governance across the teams.

**What we’re looking for:**

* Exceptional problem-solving capability: You have a proven track record of solving complex problems, thinking creatively, and using data to tell a story and drive change.

You can create and interpret complex Excel reports to track past, present, and future conference data and determine how to represent this in Power BI. Exposure to SQL, Python and Power Automate is strongly preferred.
* Detail oriented: You have a critical eye for details and can effectively analyze and summarize data.

**Role Summary**
We are seeking a Clinical Coding & Claims Analytics Consultant with experience in clinical coding, medical claims analysis, reimbursement methodologies, and healthcare consulting. The role will support the development of clinical rules for claims adjudication, conduct coding and reimbursement analytics, contribute to DRG and grouper initiatives, and deliver consulting projects for healthcare payers, providers, and health system stakeholders.
  
  
The ideal candidate should possess strong knowledge of clinical coding systems, health insurance operations, claims adjudication workflows, reimbursement frameworks, and healthcare data analytics, with exposure to healthcare markets across the Middle East.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Clinical Rules & Product Development**

* Support the design, development, testing, and validation of clinical rules used in medical claims adjudication and payment integrity programs.
* Define clinical logic for medical necessity review, coding validation, reimbursement controls, benefit interpretation, and claims editing.
* Participate in user acceptance testing (UAT) and validation of clinical rule engines and adjudication systems.

**Clinical Coding & Classification**

* Perform clinical coding reviews and code mapping across healthcare coding and classification systems - ICD-10-AM, ACHI, SBS and ADRG / AR-DRG
* Ensure coding consistency and compliance with applicable coding standards, reimbursement guidelines, and payer policies.
* Support coding validation exercises, reimbursement reviews, and clinical classification projects.

**Claims Analytics & Reimbursement**

* Analyze structured and unstructured medical claims data to identify coding discrepancies, billing anomalies, utilization patterns, and reimbursement opportunities.
* Support payment integrity initiatives through identification of inappropriate billing, coding errors, duplicate claims, and reimbursement leakage.
* Contribute to DRG grouper validation, fee schedule development, reimbursement modelling, and healthcare costing initiatives.

**Healthcare Consulting & Project Delivery**

* Support consulting projects related to:

+ Clinical code mapping
+ Claims audits
+ Claims analytics
+ DRG implementation

* Develop analytical reports, presentations, client deliverables, and documentation.
* Participate in stakeholder discussions and support project execution across multiple workstreams.

**Data Quality & Insights**

* Conduct healthcare data quality assessments and identify opportunities for process improvement.
* Interpret payer policies, reimbursement guidelines, and regulatory requirements relevant to claims adjudication and coding practices.
* Generate actionable insights from claims and clinical data to support decision-making and operational improvements.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Medicine, Dentistry, Nursing, Pharmacy, Life Sciences, Health Information Management, Healthcare Management, or a related healthcare discipline.
* HIMAA certified and working knowledge of coding systems such as ICD-10-AM, ACHI, SBS and AR-DRG.
* 2–4 years of experience in clinical coding, health insurance, claims analytics, healthcare consulting, revenue cycle management, or reimbursement analysis.
* Strong understanding of:

+ Clinical coding standards
+ Medical claims lifecycle
+ Health insurance operations
+ Claims adjudication workflows

* Experience performing claims reviews, coding audits, reimbursement analyses.
* Strong analytical, problem-solving, and documentation skills.
* Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel or similar analytics tools is preferred.
* Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary teams and manage multiple project priorities.

**Key Competencies**

* Clinical Coding & Classification
* Claims Adjudication & Payment Integrity
* Healthcare Reimbursement
* DRG & Grouper Analytics
* Claims Data Analysis
* Data Quality Assessment
* Analytical Thinking & Problem Solving
* Documentation & Communication

title: Product Associate
description:

PlaySuper is India's first Gaming Commerce company, pioneering a new way for 500M+ gamers, an audience growing at 19.6% YoY, to shop inside games.

It is a white-label SaaS plugin that integrates into casual and hyper-casual games, transforming in-game coins into real-world value. Players can redeem them for brand coupons, digital services, or even physical products inside fully customizable in-game stores.

For gaming studios, PlaySuper directly solves the industry's toughest challenge, low retention, while also boosting monetisation. For brands, it unlocks a massive high-attention audience that already spends billions on in-game experiences, enabling targeted engagement with measurable ROI. Unlike traditional ads, PlaySuper embeds commerce into gameplay itself, improving recall, conversion, and loyalty.

In under two years, PlaySuper has onboarded 20+ studios, 3,000+ brands, and reached 6M+ DAUs through its partners, backed by $1.6M funding from Jungle Ventures (Chimera), Audacity VC, IAN Capital Fund, 100x.VC, and leaders from Meta, Tata, Dyson, and Amazon.

playsuper.ai

**funnels, user behaviour, and data**

* Can pull their own data instead of waiting for someone else to

title: Senior Associate - Business Operations
description:
**About GoKwik**
GoKwik is building the growth operating system for D2C and eCommerce brands, enabling businesses to optimise checkout, reduce RTO, power payments, drive retention, and unlock post-purchase engagement. With 15,000+ merchants globally and a growing presence across India, the UK, Europe, and the US, GoKwik is building technology and financial infrastructure that powers the next generation of digital commerce.
  
  
Why This Role Matters
  
  
Efficient logistics operations are critical to delivering a seamless post-purchase experience for eCommerce merchants and their customers. As a Senior Associate – Business Operations, you will drive operational excellence across the first, middle, and last mile by managing logistics partners, monitoring performance, resolving operational challenges, and using data to improve delivery outcomes.
  
  
What You’ll Own
  
  

* End-to-End Logistics Operations: Monitor and optimise first-mile pickup, mid-mile transit, and last-mile delivery operations to ensure smooth shipment movement.
* Logistics Partner Management: Coordinate with courier and logistics partners to drive operational efficiency, timely execution, and service quality.
* Performance Monitoring: Track key metrics such as on-time pickup, delivery success rate, RTO, shipment exceptions, and SLA adherence.
* Business Reviews & SLA Governance: Conduct regular performance reviews with logistics partners, identify operational gaps, and drive corrective actions.
* Exception & Escalation Management: Proactively resolve shipment delays, damages, failed pickups, delivery issues, and other operational escalations.
* Data Analysis & Reporting: Analyse logistics data to identify trends, root causes, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
* Dashboards & MIS: Build and maintain reports and dashboards to track operational performance and support data-driven decisions.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with Technology, Customer Service, Warehouse, and internal Operations teams to resolve issues and improve workflows.
* Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve partner performance, and strengthen operational controls.

Who You Are
  
  

* Have 3–5 years of experience in eCommerce logistics, supply chain operations, courier management, or a related field.
* Understand first-mile, mid-mile, and last-mile operations and key logistics performance metrics.
* Have hands-on experience managing courier partners, monitoring SLAs, and driving performance improvements.
* Are proficient in Excel and Google Sheets, with experience using BI tools such as Power BI or Tableau.
* Can analyse operational data, identify root causes, and translate insights into actionable improvements.
* Are comfortable managing exceptions, escalations, and multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
* Have strong communication, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills.
* Demonstrate ownership, attention to detail, and a structured, data-driven approach to problem-solving.

Why GoKwik
  
  
At GoKwik, you will work on complex eCommerce logistics challenges that directly influence merchant growth and customer experience. You will have the opportunity to collaborate across teams, work closely with logistics partners, use data to drive measurable improvements, and take ownership of initiatives that make post-purchase operations more efficient and reliable.

title: Team Leader
description:

Being a Great Place to Work and providing a culture of caring is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!
  
  
**Global Business Services**
Global Business Services delivers Technology and Operations capabilities to Lines of Business and Staff Support Functions of Bank of America through a centrally managed, globally integrated delivery model and globally resilient operations.
  
  
Global Business Services is recognized for flawless execution, sound risk management, operational resiliency, operational excellence and innovation.
  
  
In India, we are present in five locations and operate as BA Continuum India Private Limited (BACI), a non-banking subsidiary of Bank of America Corporation and the operating company for India operations of Global Business Services.
  
  
**Process Overview**
Global Markets Operations & Middle Office provides operations support to the Global Markets Business of Bank of America. * Perform self-review of data input in the back-office systems. Ability to perform checks in order to maintain control and maintain process accuracy.
* Work on projects and special assignments and provide SME support.
* Ensure that all established procedures are followed
* Excellent organizational skills are required with the ability to prioritize workload, work accurately and efficiently under pressure

**Education**
: Graduate/B.Com, Preferably Masters in Business Administration (MBA) - Finance
